name: Hekaton
tagline: SQL Server's built-in lock-free, memory-optimized OLTP engine with natively compiled T-SQL.
description: Hekaton is the code name for In-Memory OLTP, the memory-optimized transaction engine built into Microsoft SQL Server since 2014 and available in Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance. Tables declared MEMORY_OPTIMIZED live entirely in RAM with hash or Bw-tree indexes, and use multi-version optimistic concurrency with no locks or latches; T-SQL stored procedures, triggers and scalar functions can be compiled to native machine code. Tables are fully durable through the transaction log by default, or can be declared SCHEMA_ONLY to skip I/O for session state and staging data. Because it lives inside SQL Server, memory-optimized and disk-based tables can be joined in one query and share backups and availability groups.

license.name: Included with Microsoft SQL Server licensing

pricing.notes: Part of SQL Server editions (including free Express and Developer) and supported Azure SQL tiers.

scale.notes: Memory-optimized data must fit in the server's RAM; scale-out and DR come from SQL Server availability groups.

strengths: Lock- and latch-free multi-version concurrency removes contention hot spots
Natively compiled stored procedures cut CPU per transaction
SCHEMA_ONLY tables give no-I/O temp tables, staging tables and session state
Mix memory-optimized and disk-based tables in the same database and query
Works with SQL Server backups, availability groups and failover clusters
weaknesses: All memory-optimized data must fit in RAM and needs careful memory sizing
Natively compiled modules support a restricted T-SQL surface
Optimistic concurrency means write conflicts abort and need retry logic
Only available inside SQL Server and Azure SQL
useCases: High-throughput order, trading or betting transactions
ASP.NET session state and mid-tier caching
Replacing tempdb table variables and temp tables
notIdealFor: Data sets bigger than server memory
